docs.title: Kartoza CloudBench
docs.text: A comprehensive cloud-native geospatial data management platform with TUI (Terminal User Interface) and Web UI for managing GeoServer, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, S3 storage, and more.

docs.title: Web UI
docs.text:
• Modern React interface - Beautiful Chakra UI-based web application
  • Tree browser - Hierarchical view of all GeoServer resources
  • Layer metadata editing - Comprehensive metadata management
  • GeoWebCache management - Seed, reseed, and truncate cached tiles
  • Map preview - Interactive map preview with WMS/WMTS support
  • Chunked file upload - Upload large geospatial files with progress tracking
  • S3 Storage integration - Browse and manage cloud-native geospatial data

docs.title: TUI (Terminal User Interface)
docs.text:
• Textual-based interface - Modern Python TUI with rich widgets
  • Connection manager - Store and manage multiple GeoServer connections
  • Vim-style navigation - Familiar keyboard shortcuts

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• GeoServer - Full REST API management
  • PostgreSQL/PostGIS - Direct database connections
  • S3/MinIO - Cloud storage for geospatial data
  • QGIS Server - Project management and preview
  • Terria/Cesium - 3D globe visualization

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench.git
cd kartoza-cloudbench

# Using Nix (recommended)
nix develop
python manage.py runserver 8080

# Or using pip
pip install -e .
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py runserver 8080

Then visit http://localhost:8080

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
CloudBench is built with:

  • Backend: Python/Django with Django REST Framework
  • Frontend: React with Chakra UI and Zustand state management
  • TUI: Python Textual framework
  • Maps: MapLibre GL JS with CARTO basemaps

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: This guide covers deploying CloudBench in production environments.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • PostgreSQL 14+ (recommended for production)
  • Reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, etc.)

docs.title: 1. Clone and Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench.git
cd kartoza-cloudbench
pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. Configure Environment
docs.text:
Create /etc/cloudbench/env:

DEBUG=false
SECRET_KEY=your-secure-random-key-here
ALLOWED_HOSTS=cloudbench.example.com
DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/cloudbench

docs.title: 3. Database Setup
docs.text:
# Create database
createdb cloudbench

# Run migrations
python manage.py migrate

# Create admin user
python manage.py createsuperuser

docs.title: 4. Collect Static Files
docs.text: python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

docs.title: 5. Run with Gunicorn
docs.text:
gunicorn cloudbench.wsgi:application \
    --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 \
    --workers 4 \
    --threads 2

docs.title: 6. Nginx Configuration
docs.text:
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name cloudbench.example.com;

    location /static/ {
        alias /path/to/cloudbench/staticfiles/;
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

docs.title: Systemd Service
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/cloudbench.service:

[Unit]
Description=CloudBench Web Application
After=network.target postgresql.service

[Service]
User=cloudbench
Group=cloudbench
WorkingDirectory=/opt/cloudbench
EnvironmentFile=/etc/cloudbench/env
ExecStart=/opt/cloudbench/venv/bin/gunicorn cloudbench.wsgi:application --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --workers 4
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable and start:

systemctl enable cloudbench
systemctl start cloudbench

docs.title: Security Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Set DEBUG=false
  • [ ] Use strong SECRET_KEY
  • [ ] Configure HTTPS
  • [ ] Set proper ALLOWED_HOSTS
  • [ ] Use PostgreSQL (not SQLite)
  • [ ] Configure firewall
  • [ ] Set up log rotation

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text: CloudBench can be deployed using Docker and Docker Compose.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: docker compose up -d

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'

services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - DEBUG=false
      - SECRET_KEY=${SECRET_KEY}
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@db:5432/cloudbench
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:16-3.4
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=cloudbench
      - POSTGRES_USER=postgres
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  postgres_data:

docs.title: Building the Image
docs.text: docker build -t ghcr.io/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench:latest .

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Pass environment variables via:

docker run -e SECRET_KEY=xxx -e DEBUG=false ghcr.io/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench

Or use an env file:

docker run --env-file .env ghcr.io/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Complete reference of CloudBench environment variables.

docs.title: Django Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default SECRET_KEY Django secret key Auto-generated DEBUG Enable debug mode true ALLOWED_HOSTS Comma-separated hosts localhost,127.0.0.1

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Variable Description Default DATABASE_URL Database URL sqlite:///db.sqlite3

Format: postgres://user:password@host:port/dbname

docs.title: Upload Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE Max upload bytes 10737418240 (10GB) UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE Chunk size bytes 5242880 (5MB)

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Variable Description Default CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS Trusted origins Empty CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS CORS origins http://localhost:*

docs.title: Example .env File
docs.text:
# Production settings
DEBUG=false
SECRET_KEY=your-very-long-random-secret-key-here
ALLOWED_HOSTS=cloudbench.example.com,www.cloudbench.example.com
DATABASE_URL=postgres://cloudbench:password@localhost:5432/cloudbench

# Upload settings
UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE=10737418240

# Security
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://cloudbench.example.com

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: CloudBench exposes a REST API under /api/.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Currently, the API supports session authentication. API tokens are planned.

docs.title: List Connections
docs.text:
GET /api/connections

Response: 

[
  {
    "id": "conn_123",
    "name": "Local GeoServer",
    "url": "http://localhost:8600/geoserver",
    "is_active": true
  }
]

docs.title: Create Connection
docs.text:
POST /api/connections
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "My GeoServer",
  "url": "http://geoserver.example.com/geoserver",
  "username": "admin",
  "password": "geoserver"
}

docs.title: List Workspaces
docs.text: GET /api/workspaces/{conn_id}

docs.title: Create Workspace
docs.text:
POST /api/workspaces/{conn_id}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "my_workspace"
}

docs.title: List Layers
docs.text: GET /api/layers/{conn_id}/{workspace}

docs.title: Get Layer Details
docs.text: GET /api/layers/{conn_id}/{workspace}/{layer}

docs.title: Get Layer Styles
docs.text:
GET /api/layerstyles/{conn_id}/{workspace}/{layer}

Response: 

{
  "defaultStyle": "polygon",
  "additionalStyles": ["line", "point"]
}

docs.title: Start Preview Session
docs.text:
POST /api/preview/
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "connId": "conn_123",
  "workspace": "topp",
  "layerName": "states"
}

Response: 

{
  "url": "/api/preview/abc-123"
}

docs.title: Get Layer Info
docs.text: GET /api/preview/{session_id}/api/layer

docs.title: Get Layer Metadata
docs.text: GET /api/preview/{session_id}/api/metadata

docs.title: Initialize Upload
docs.text:
POST /api/upload/init
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "connectionId": "conn_123",
  "workspace": "topp",
  "filename": "data.gpkg",
  "fileSize": 1048576,
  "chunkSize": 5242880
}

docs.title: Upload Chunk
docs.text:
POST /api/upload/chunk
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

sessionId: abc-123
chunkIndex: 0
chunk: <binary data>

docs.title: Complete Upload
docs.text:
POST /api/upload/complete
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sessionId": "abc-123"
}

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
All errors return JSON:

{
  "error": "Description of the error"
}

HTTP status codes: - 400: Bad request - 401: Unauthorized - 404: Not found - 500: Server error

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: CloudBench can be configured through environment variables and configuration files.

docs.title: Django Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default SECRET_KEY Django secret key Auto-generated DEBUG Enable debug mode true ALLOWED_HOSTS Comma-separated allowed hosts localhost,127.0.0.1

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Variable Description Default DATABASE_URL Database connection URL SQLite

Example: 

export DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/cloudbench

docs.title: Upload Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE Maximum upload size in bytes 10737418240 (10GB)

docs.title: PostgreSQL Services
docs.text:
PostgreSQL connections are configured via the standard ~/.pg_service.conf file:

[production]
host=db.example.com
port=5432
dbname=geodata
user=geouser
password=secret

[development]
host=localhost
port=5432
dbname=geodata_dev
user=postgres
password=postgres

These services appear in the CloudBench sidebar under "PostgreSQL Services".

docs.title: GeoServer Connections
docs.text:
GeoServer connections are stored in the database and can be managed through:

  1. Web UI: Click the + button next to "GeoServer Connections"
  2. Admin Panel: Visit /admin/ to manage connections
  3. API: POST to /api/connections

docs.title: S3 Storage
docs.text:
S3/MinIO connections can be added through the Web UI:

  1. Click + next to "S3 Storage"
  2. Enter:
  3. Name: Connection name
  4. Endpoint: S3 endpoint URL
  5. Access Key: AWS access key
  6. Secret Key: AWS secret key
  7. Region: AWS region (optional)

docs.title: Development Settings
docs.text:
For development, create a .env file in the project root:

DEBUG=true
SECRET_KEY=dev-secret-key-change-in-production
ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1

docs.title: Production Settings
docs.text:
For production deployments:

DEBUG=false
SECRET_KEY=your-secure-random-key
ALLOWED_HOSTS=your-domain.com
DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@db:5432/cloudbench

See Deployment Guide for more details.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or higher
  • Node.js 22 or higher (for frontend development)
  • PostgreSQL (optional, for production database)

docs.title: Using Nix (Recommended)
docs.text:
The easiest way to get started is using Nix, which provides a reproducible development environment with all dependencies.

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench.git
cd kartoza-cloudbench

# Enter the development shell
nix develop

# Run database migrations
python manage.py migrate

# Start the development server
python manage.py runserver 8080

docs.title: Using pip
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/kartoza/kartoza-cloudbench.git
cd kartoza-cloudbench

# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install the package
pip install -e .

# Run database migrations
python manage.py migrate

# Build the frontend (optional, pre-built assets included)
cd web
npm install
npm run build
cd ..

# Start the server
python manage.py runserver 8080

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Build and run with Docker Compose
docker compose up -d

See Docker Deployment for detailed instructions.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide will help you get CloudBench running and connected to your first GeoServer instance.

docs.title: 1. Start the Server
docs.text:
# Using Nix
nix develop
python manage.py runserver 8080

# Or using pip
python manage.py runserver 8080

docs.title: 2. Open the Web UI
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8080 in your browser.

docs.title: 3. Add a GeoServer Connection
docs.text:
1. In the left sidebar, find "GeoServer Connections"
  2. Click the + button to add a new connection
  3. Enter your GeoServer details:
  4. Name: A friendly name for this connection
  5. URL: Your GeoServer URL (e.g., http://localhost:8600/geoserver)
  6. Username: GeoServer admin username
  7. Password: GeoServer admin password
  8. Click Test Connection to verify
  9. Click Save to add the connection

docs.title: 4. Browse Your Data
docs.text:
Once connected, you can:

  • Expand workspaces to see data stores, coverage stores, and layers
  • Click on a layer to see its details in the right panel
  • Preview layers on an interactive map
  • Upload data to create new stores and layers

docs.title: 5. Upload Geospatial Data
docs.text:
1. Select a workspace in the tree
  2. Click the Upload button (arrow icon)
  3. Select your file (Shapefile ZIP, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, etc.)
  4. The file will be uploaded and published automatically

docs.title: 6. Preview Layers
docs.text:
1. Click on any layer in the tree
  2. Click the Preview button (eye icon)
  3. An interactive map will appear showing your layer

docs.title: Using the TUI
docs.text:
CloudBench also includes a terminal user interface:

python -m tui

Navigate using: - j/k or ↑/↓: Move up/down - Enter: Select/expand - Tab: Switch panels - q: Quit

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Web UI Guide - Learn all Web UI features
  • GeoServer Management - Manage workspaces, stores, and layers
  • Configuration - Customize CloudBench settings

docs.title: GeoServer Management
docs.text: CloudBench provides comprehensive management of GeoServer instances through the REST API.

docs.title: Creating a Workspace
docs.text:
1. Right-click on "Workspaces" in a connection
  2. Select "New Workspace"
  3. Enter workspace name
  4. Configure options:
  5. Default workspace
  6. Isolated workspace

docs.title: Workspace Settings
docs.text:
• Services: Enable/disable OGC services (WMS, WFS, WCS, WMTS)
  • Security: Workspace-level access control

docs.title: Supported Types
docs.text: Type Description PostGIS PostgreSQL/PostGIS database Shapefile Single shapefile or directory GeoPackage OGC GeoPackage file WFS External WFS service

docs.title: Creating a Data Store
docs.text:
1. Select a workspace
  2. Click "Add Data Store"
  3. Choose store type
  4. Enter connection parameters
  5. Click "Save"

docs.title: PostGIS Connection
docs.text:
Host: localhost
Port: 5432
Database: geodata
Schema: public
User: postgres
Password: ********

docs.title: Supported Types
docs.text: Type Description GeoTIFF Single GeoTIFF file Image Mosaic Directory of images Image Pyramid Multi-resolution pyramid WorldImage Image with world file

docs.title: Layer Properties
docs.text:
• Enabled: Layer serves requests
  • Advertised: Layer in GetCapabilities
  • Queryable: Supports GetFeatureInfo

docs.title: Bounding Boxes
docs.text:
• Native bounding box (original CRS)
  • Lat/Lon bounding box (EPSG:4326)
  • Auto-compute from data

docs.title: Styles
docs.text:
• Default style
  • Additional styles
  • Style preview in layer viewer

docs.title: Layer Groups
docs.text:
Combine multiple layers into a single requestable group:

  1. Select workspace
  2. Click "New Layer Group"
  3. Add layers to the group
  4. Configure bounds and styles

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text:
• SLD: Styled Layer Descriptor (XML)
  • CSS: GeoServer CSS extension

docs.title: Uploading Styles
docs.text:
1. Go to Styles section
  2. Click "Upload Style"
  3. Select SLD or CSS file
  4. Style is available for layer assignment

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Organize with workspaces: Group related layers
  2. Use meaningful names: Clear, descriptive resource names
  3. Set bounding boxes: Improves performance
  4. Enable caching: Use GeoWebCache for production

docs.title: Layer Preview
docs.text: CloudBench includes an interactive map viewer for previewing layers.

docs.title: Starting a Preview
docs.text:
1. Click on a layer in the tree browser
  2. Click the Preview button (eye icon)
  3. The map preview opens in the main content area

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Pan: Click and drag
  • Zoom: Scroll wheel or +/- buttons
  • Rotate (3D mode): Ctrl + drag

docs.title: View Modes
docs.text: Mode Description 2D Standard flat map view 3D Tilted perspective view Globe Full 3D Cesium globe

docs.title: Style Selection
docs.text:
The preview includes a style picker:

  1. Click the style dropdown in the header
  2. Select from available styles
  3. Map updates immediately
  4. Legend icons show style preview

docs.title: Layer Information
docs.text:
Click the Info button to see:

  • Layer title and abstract
  • Coordinate reference system
  • Bounding box
  • Enabled/advertised status

docs.title: Basemap
docs.text:
The preview uses CARTO basemaps:

  • Light theme for clear visibility
  • Attribution included

docs.title: WMS Parameters
docs.text:
The preview uses WMS for layer display:

  • Format: PNG with transparency
  • SRS: EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator)
  • Tiled: 256x256 tiles

docs.title: 3D Globe Preview
docs.text:
For 3D visualization:

  1. Click the Globe button
  2. Opens Cesium-based viewer
  3. Full 3D terrain and imagery
  4. Layer draped on terrain

docs.title: Blank Preview
docs.text:
1. Check GeoServer is accessible
  2. Verify layer is enabled
  3. Check browser console for errors

docs.title: Wrong Location
docs.text:
1. Verify layer bounding box
  2. Check coordinate system settings
  3. Ensure data is georeferenced

docs.title: TUI Guide
docs.text: CloudBench includes a Terminal User Interface (TUI) built with Python Textual.

docs.title: Starting the TUI
docs.text:
python -m tui

Or using the Nix shortcut: 

runtui

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Key Action ↑ / k Move up ↓ / j Move down Enter / l Select / Expand Backspace / h Go back / Collapse Tab Switch panels q / Ctrl+C Quit

docs.title: Connection Manager
docs.text: Key Action a Add connection e Edit connection d Delete connection t Test connection Enter Connect

docs.title: GeoServer Browser
docs.text:
• Browse workspaces, stores, and layers
  • View resource metadata
  • Expand/collapse tree nodes

docs.title: Connection Management
docs.text:
• Store multiple GeoServer connections
  • Credentials securely stored
  • Quick connect/disconnect

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The TUI supports token-based authentication:

  1. On first run, enter your credentials
  2. A token is saved to ~/.config/kartoza-cloudbench/auth.json
  3. Subsequent runs use the saved token

To logout: 

rm ~/.config/kartoza-cloudbench/auth.json

docs.title: File Uploads
docs.text: CloudBench supports uploading geospatial data files directly to GeoServer.

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text: Type Extensions Target Shapefile .zip Data Store GeoPackage .gpkg Data Store GeoTIFF .tif, .tiff Coverage Store GeoJSON .geojson, .json Data Store SLD Style .sld Styles CSS Style .css Styles

docs.title: Via Web UI
docs.text:
1. Select a workspace in the tree
  2. Click the Upload button (arrow icon)
  3. Select your file
  4. Monitor upload progress
  5. Layer is automatically published

docs.title: Chunked Uploads
docs.text:
Large files are automatically uploaded in chunks:

  • Default chunk size: 5 MB
  • Progress tracking per chunk
  • Resume capability on failure
  • Files up to 10 GB supported

docs.title: Upload Process
docs.text:
1. Initialize: Create upload session
  2. Upload chunks: Send file in pieces
  3. Assemble: Combine chunks on server
  4. Publish: Create store and layer in GeoServer

docs.title: Shapefile Requirements
docs.text:
When uploading shapefiles:

  • Package as a ZIP file
  • Include all required files:
  • .shp - Shape geometry
  • .shx - Shape index
  • .dbf - Attributes
  • .prj - Projection (recommended)

docs.title: GeoPackage
docs.text:
GeoPackage files can contain:

  • Multiple vector layers
  • Raster tiles
  • Feature attributes

All layers in the GeoPackage are published.

docs.title: GeoTIFF
docs.text:
GeoTIFF requirements:

  • Embedded or external georeferencing
  • Supported pixel types
  • Optional internal tiling for performance

docs.title: Upload Fails
docs.text:
1. Check file size limits
  2. Verify file format is supported
  3. Check GeoServer logs for errors

docs.title: Layer Not Visible
docs.text:
1. Verify layer is enabled
  2. Check coordinate system
  3. Validate bounding box

docs.title: Web UI Guide
docs.text: The CloudBench Web UI provides a modern, intuitive interface for managing your geospatial infrastructure.

docs.title: Interface Overview
docs.text:
The interface is divided into three main areas:

  1. Left Sidebar - Tree browser for all resources
  2. Main Content - Details panel, map preview, or data views
  3. Header - Search, settings, and user info

docs.title: Tree Browser
docs.text: The tree browser shows all your connected resources:

docs.title: GeoServer Connections
docs.text:
• Workspaces
  • Data Stores (vector data)
  • Coverage Stores (raster data)
  • Layers
  • Styles
  • Layer Groups

docs.title: PostgreSQL Services
docs.text:
• Schemas
  • Tables (with geometry info)

docs.title: S3 Storage
docs.text:
• Buckets
  • Objects (folders and files)

docs.title: QGIS Projects
docs.text: • Registered QGIS Server projects

docs.title: Adding a Connection
docs.text:
1. Click + next to "GeoServer Connections"
  2. Fill in the connection details
  3. Click Test Connection to verify
  4. Click Save

docs.title: Managing Workspaces
docs.text:
• Create: Right-click workspace list → New Workspace
  • Edit: Click workspace → Edit button
  • Delete: Click workspace → Delete button

docs.title: Uploading Data
docs.text:
1. Select a workspace
  2. Click the Upload button
  3. Select your file:
  4. Shapefile (.zip)
  5. GeoPackage (.gpkg)
  6. GeoTIFF (.tif, .tiff)
  7. GeoJSON (.geojson)
  8. Large files are uploaded in chunks with progress tracking

docs.title: Layer Preview
docs.text:
1. Click on a layer in the tree
  2. Click the Preview button (eye icon)
  3. The map preview shows:
  4. Interactive map with CARTO basemap
  5. Your layer via WMS
  6. Layer metadata panel
  7. Style selector

docs.title: Managing Styles
docs.text:
• View available styles for each layer
  • Switch between styles in the preview
  • Upload new SLD or CSS styles

docs.title: View Modes
docs.text:
• 2D - Standard flat map view
  • 3D - Tilted perspective view
  • Globe - Full 3D Cesium globe

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Pan: Click and drag
  • Zoom: Scroll wheel
  • Rotate (3D): Ctrl + drag

docs.title: Style Picker
docs.text:
• Click the style dropdown to change layer styling
  • Preview shows legend icons for each style

docs.title: GeoWebCache
docs.text:
Manage tile caching for your layers:

  1. Select a layer
  2. Open the GWC panel
  3. Choose operation:
  4. Seed: Generate new tiles
  5. Reseed: Regenerate existing tiles
  6. Truncate: Clear cached tiles
  7. Monitor progress in real-time
